newsitem.title: BELGIUM: French fast food tax plan hits Belgian Quick shares.
newsitem.headline: French fast food tax plan hits Belgian Quick shares.

text.p: Shares in Belgian hamburger chain operator Quick plunged on the Brussels bourse on Thursday on news of a French proposal for a "Big Mac Tax."

At one point shares in Quick, a major player in France and Belgium, were down nine percent at 2,150 Belgian francs, a 1996 low, before recovering slightly to close at 2,190 francs, down 175 on the day.

Analysts said further losses were likely if the French government accepted the proposal from its parliamentary finance committee to raise the Value Added Tax (VAT) rate on fast food to 20.6 from 5.5 percent.
"After the severe impact of the scare around mad cow disease this could be another blow for Quick and its parent company GIB," Generale Bank said in an investor note.
France accounts for two-thirds of Quick's sales and earnings and the company is in the middle of a programme to raise the number of its retail outlets there.
Quick opened 22 new stores in the first six months of 1996, 15 of which were in France.
"(A tax) would be very disappointing. France is an important market for Quick," BBL analyst Ann Vanhelmont said.

"The French government needs all the money it can get and I'm sure something is going to happen, especially when you consider that (regular) restaurants are already taxed at 20 percent," one trader said. "It's going to cost (Quick) a lot of money."
Quick's share has lost a third of its value this year because of Europe's mad cow crisis. The company warned last month 1996 profit could fall by up to 35 percent because of the beef scare.
